review_note: Compared against pinned, proof-masked examples.tex L6566 and its logical scope: Localization Mod_A→Mod_{S^{-1}A} is exact with kernel the Serre subcategory of S-torsion modules, and universal for annihilating that subcategory, hence induces the claimed canonical Serre quotient equivalence. Both categories are preserved.
statement:
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $A$.
Let $\text{Mod}_A$ denote the category of $A$-modules and $\mathcal{T}$ its
Serre subcategory of modules for which any element is annihilated by some
element of $S$. Then there is a canonical equivalence
$\text{Mod}_A/\mathcal{T} \rightarrow \text{Mod}_{S^{-1}A}$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-localization-and-serre-quotients}
Let $A$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a multiplicative subset of $A$.
Let $\text{Mod}_A$ denote the category of $A$-modules and $\mathcal{T}$ its
Serre subcategory of modules for which any element is annihilated by some
element of $S$. Then there is a canonical equivalence
$\text{Mod}_A/\mathcal{T} \rightarrow \text{Mod}_{S^{-1}A}$.

review_note: Compared against pinned, proof-masked examples.tex L6619 and its logical scope: For a Noetherian domain A, tensoring finitely generated modules with fraction field K kills precisely finitely generated torsion modules and identifies the Serre quotient with finite-dimensional K-vector spaces. The fg and Noetherian assumptions remain.
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Let $K$ denote its field of fractions.
Let $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}$ denote the category of finitely generated $A$-modules
and $\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ its Serre subcategory of finitely generated torsion
modules. Then $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}/\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ is canonically equivalent
to the category of finite dimensional $K$-vector spaces.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-quotient-by-finitely-generated-torsion-modules}
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Let $K$ denote its field of fractions.
Let $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}$ denote the category of finitely generated $A$-modules
and $\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ its Serre subcategory of finitely generated torsion
modules. Then $\text{Mod}_A^{fg}/\mathcal{T}^{fg}$ is canonically equivalent
to the category of finite dimensional $K$-vector spaces.

review_note: Compared against pinned, proof-masked examples.tex L6642 and its logical scope: The category of abelian groups localized by all torsion groups is equivalent to rational vector spaces, since rationalization Q⊗_Z− is exact with torsion kernel and essentially surjective. It is an unconditional category-equivalence assertion.
statement:
The quotient of the category of abelian groups modulo its
Serre subcategory of torsion groups is the category of
$\mathbf{Q}$-vector spaces.
conclusions:
The quotient of the category of abelian groups modulo its
Serre subcategory of torsion groups is the category of
$\mathbf{Q}$-vector spaces.
